cashReason: CASH — the one qualifying catalyst repriced past the entry band before the run. Forgent Power Solutions (NYSE: FPS) was the single name on the board with a fresh, company-specific, this-morning catalyst: fiscal Q4 reported before the open with EPS of $0.309 vs. $0.24 consensus, a ~29% beat, in a company that designs electrical distribution equipment for data centers and the power grid. The setup was genuinely asymmetric on paper — the stock closed at $28.64, down 53% from its June 22 high of $66 and only $2.69 above its 52-week low of $25.95, beaten down mostly by two upsized equity offerings (May 28 and July 1) rather than fundamentals, against a record $1.98B backlog (+157% YoY), bookings +308% YoY to $867M, FY26 revenue guided to +82% growth, a footprint being built toward $5B of annual capacity, and Street price targets of $51 (Morgan Stanley), $55 (Baird, Barclays) and $60 (Goldman, Oppenheimer). But the entry is gone. FPS was quoted $31.27 (+9.2%) at 10:36Z, $31.75 (+10.9%) at 10:38Z and $31.78 (+11.0%) at 10:39Z — climbing, not fading, and past the mandate's do-not-chase band of 8-10%. At that price the stop math breaks: a 5-7% stop sits at $29.53-$30.16, while the pre-market low is $28.81 and the prior close is $28.64, so an ordinary post-earnings gap-fade — the modal 24-hour outcome for an +11% earnings gapper — is -9.8% from entry and blows straight through any stop I could set. That is risking 6-10% to make 3-5%, the inverse of the mandate. Two further disciplines failed: I could not read the actual Q4 revenue line or the FY27 guidance (the IR page, the SEC submissions feed and the news indexes are all still cached pre-release, so the only hard datapoint is the EPS actual plus the price reaction), and the canonical price could not be cross-verified — the dashboard's Yahoo feed returned FPS at $28.64 with a fresh asOf of 10:39:30Z, i.e. the prior close dressed as a live quote, which is exactly the stale-quote trap. Going 100% all-in on a print I have not read, at +11%, on a single-sourced price, is momentum-following, not underwriting. Nothing else qualifies. The read-through to data-center power peers is unpriced but derived, not company-specific: VRT $238.91 (+0.64%), GEV $877 (+0.26%), PWR $622.99 (+0.16%), ETN and BE flat, and the rest of the complex (POWL, NVT, HUBB, ATKR, AOS, MOD, TT) shows placeholder pre-market spreads of 5-13% with no real two-sided market. GEV's Bernstein Outperform at a $1,298 target is an opinion, not new fact. The entire pre-market gainer list is sub-$6 micro-caps — BDRX, MYSZ, VEEA, ADBT, TNON, FTFT — all disqualified as penny/illiquid. Energy is nine sessions into its run with Brent near $108 and WTI above $103; buying that is chasing a geopolitical premium one Iran headline unwinds, and XOM just had a power outage at its Joliet refinery. ENVA at -18% is a loser, not a long. TCOM and LEN report after my exit window. The macro backdrop argues the same way for a levered, capex-heavy industrial long: the FOMC's two-day meeting opens today with an ~88.5% chance of a HIKE priced, the 10-year topped 5% intraday Monday for the first time since 2023, German ZEW came in at 25.8 vs. 39.9 expected, and industrials was the worst S&P sector Monday. SPY -0.35%, QQQ -0.33%, DIA -0.47%, IWM -0.37% pre-market. This book is down 33.6% from inception largely from buying the second half of a move; passing on an +11% gap preserves $6,635.79 for a day with a real entry. Re-evaluating at Wednesday's 6:35am CT run, which lands before the FOMC decision that afternoon — and FPS goes on the watchlist for a pullback toward the $29 gap.
